p21-l01.q: What is the one thing a cable cannot do?
p21-l01.explain: A cable in compression goes slack. Every design choice in a CDPR follows from that.

p21-l01.q: How many cables must surround a point to hold it against a force from any direction, with no gravity to help?
p21-l01.explain: n + 1 for n degrees of freedom. With three, some direction cannot be resisted with positive tensions.

p21-l01.q: Why can Stringman hold its gripper with four cables even though they all meet at one point?
p21-l01.explain: A suspended robot uses its own weight as the restoring force.
options: The motors push as well as pull
The anchors are at different heights
Gravity always pulls down, acting like an extra cable that never goes slack

p21-l01.q: Stringman’s work volume per $1,000 for a 7 × 7 × 3 m room at $795 (m³)?
What did NIST’s RoboCrane gain by using six cables to three points instead of one hook?
p21-l01.explain: A single-point crane resists swing and twist poorly; six cables fix all six degrees of freedom.
options: Control of the platform’s full pose, so it no longer swings or twists freely

p21-l02.q: Length of line 2 from anchor (3.5, −3.5, 3) to a pivot at (1.0, −0.5, 0.9) (m)?
Rate of change of that line when the pivot moves at 0.4 m/s in +x (m/s)?
p21-l02.explain: −u·v, with the x component of (p − a)/l equal to −2.5/4.434.

p21-l02.q: What is row i of the length Jacobian dl/dp?
options: Minus the unit vector from the pivot to anchor i
The cross product of two cable directions

p21-l02.q: You want Stringman’s fingers at a point on the floor. Where do you aim the pivot?
p21-l02.explain: The gripper hangs on a 50 cm pole below the pivot.

p21-l02.q: The forward-kinematics residual jumps to several centimetres. What is the most likely cause?
options: The robot is at the centre
A line has slipped or gone slack, so the lengths no longer agree

p21-l02.q: At the room centre, height where lifting at 0.4 m/s needs 0.2 m/s of winch speed per line (m)?

p21-l03.q: Tension in each line at the centre of a 7 × 7 × 3 m room with the pivot at 1.5 m and 1.25 kg (N)?
p21-l03.explain: m g / (4 sin θ) with sin θ = 1.5/5.172.

p21-l03.q: What does moving along the null vector do at the centre of a square room?
p21-l03.explain: n ∝ (1, −1, 1, −1); the net force does not change.
options: Tightens one diagonal pair and loosens the other

p21-l03.q: Why can’t a robot with all four anchors above the payload be pretensioned?
p21-l03.explain: All lines can only pull upwards; gravity provides the tension.
options: Every null-space direction has mixed signs, so no internal force tightens all lines at once

p21-l03.q: The minimum-norm tensions at a pose have one negative entry, and the feasible interval for λ is empty. What does that mean?
p21-l03.explain: An empty interval means there is no all-pulling solution; one line would have to push.
options: No combination of pulling cables can hold the load there

p21-l03.q: Lowest possible peak tension at the pivot (1.0, −0.5, 0.9) with 1.25 kg (N)?
p21-l03.explain: The minimax choice, with lines 2 and 3 equal at the peak.

p21-l03.q: With a position-controlled four-line robot at the centre, one line is commanded 1 mm too long. How many lines are left carrying the load in the ideal rigid model?
p21-l03.explain: Three lines fix the point; the fourth goes slack.

p21-l04.q: Capacity at the centre of the 7 × 7 × 3 m room, gripper on the floor (pivot 0.5 m), with a 28 N limit (kg)?
p21-l04.explain: 4 T sin θ / g with sin θ = 2.5/5.545.

p21-l04.q: You lower the tension limit from 28 N to 14 N. What happens to the capacity map?
p21-l04.explain: Tensions scale with the mass, so capacity is linear in the limit.
options: Nothing, capacity depends only on geometry

p21-l04.q: Close under the ceiling, where does a four-line robot hold the most?
p21-l04.explain: At the centre the lines are nearly flat there; under an anchor one line can take the whole load.
options: Under an anchor, where one line hangs nearly vertical

p21-l04.q: Capacity at the centre with the pivot at 1.5 m and a 28 N limit (kg)?
The capacity of the lines is 3 kg at a point and the gripper weighs 0.6 kg. What can it pick up there?
p21-l04.explain: Everything that hangs counts against the same tensions.

p21-l04.q: In the point-mass model, what working tension per line gives 2 kg at the floor centre (N)?

p21-l05.q: Line tension from 1 N·m on an empty 72 mm diameter spool (N)?
Motor speed for 0.4 m/s of line on that spool (rpm)?
Length of line per count of a 12-bit encoder on a 72 mm spool (mm)?
Why does Stringman’s firmware use an exponential relation between motor angle and wound length?
p21-l05.explain: ds/dθ = π D(s) with D linear in s.
options: The diameter grows linearly with line wound on, so wound length grows exponentially with angle

p21-l05.q: What must you subtract from the measured motor torque before dividing by the radius to get tension?
p21-l05.explain: Friction differs from unit to unit and in Stringman’s measurements was worth up to about 0.9 N.
options: The gravity torque of the spool
The motor’s own holding or friction torque

p21-l05.q: What is the main reason to use direct drive for a cable robot’s winches?
p21-l05.explain: No gearbox friction in between, and the drive is back-drivable.
options: Torque becomes a usable tension estimate and the line can be pulled off by hand when relaxed

p21-l06.q: A suspended four-line robot winds its lines to lengths from a model. Where does the gripper come to rest?
p21-l06.explain: Gravity pulls it down until the lines stop it; usually three are taut.
options: At the lowest point no further from each real anchor than its line
Directly under the centre of the room

p21-l06.q: The lines rise at sin θ = 0.375 and a line is 6.6 cm too short. Roughly how far does the gripper rise to make up the length (cm)?
p21-l06.explain: To first order, Δz = Δl / sin θ.

p21-l06.q: Your calibration says the ceiling is 5 cm lower than it is. What do you see?
p21-l06.explain: A common height error is a pure translation.
options: The whole workspace shifted up by 5 cm

p21-l06.q: Which pair of unknowns is hardest to tell apart in an anchor calibration?
p21-l06.explain: Both change the reading by the same amount until the line direction changes.
options: The payload and the tension limit
An anchor’s position along its own line and that line’s counter offset
The x and y of the gripper

p21-l06.explain: It takes seconds and fixes slight slack, not anchor errors.
options: Tightens the lines and resets the line-length counters from what the cameras see

p21-l06.q: The calibration residual is 1 mm, the same as the measurement noise. What does that prove?
p21-l06.explain: Poorly spread poses can give a small residual and a wrong answer.
options: Only that the model can explain the data, not that the anchors are right

p21-l07.q: Swing amplitude after a sudden stop from 0.4 m/s on that pole (cm)?
p21-l07.explain: The gripper keeps 0.4 m/s; amplitude is v/ω.

p21-l07.q: How much time does a zero-vibration shaper add to a move for that pole (s)?
Which law on the pivot’s acceleration damps the swing?
p21-l07.explain: It turns the −a coupling into −k_d d’, a damping term.
options: a = k_d d’, towards the direction the gripper is moving

p21-l07.q: Why does Stringman project its fitted swing state forward before computing the correction?
p21-l07.explain: The projection is by the measured round-trip latency.
options: To make the correction land in phase despite the delay between measuring and moving

p21-l07.q: What does a ZV shaper do about a swing started by someone bumping the gripper?
options: It damps it in half a period
Nothing; it only shapes commanded moves

p21-l08.q: What mass has a weight of 28 N (kg)?
Most force a line at 28 N can press on a body it wraps around, bent 90° on each side (N)?
A 15 N push is applied suddenly to a hanging 1.25 kg gripper. How does the peak pole force compare with the steady value?
p21-l08.explain: 33.6 N against 19.4 N in the undamped model.
options: About 1.7 times higher, because the swing overshoots

p21-l08.q: Kinetic energy of a 1.25 kg gripper dropped from 2.5 m when it reaches the floor (J)?
Which of these does a 28 N line-tension limit NOT protect against?
p21-l08.explain: At the spool the force comes from the motor torque directly.
options: A finger pinched at a spool
A line bent around a wrist
The gripper pushing hard on a person

p21-l08.explain: An unlatched stop oscillates between trip and recovery.
options: Otherwise it re-tightens into the same fault as soon as relaxing lowers the tension

p21-l09.q: Phase lag of a 0.5 m swing for a 200 ms loop delay (degrees)?
Data rate of a 2 × 2 state of 4-byte floats sent at 100 Hz (kB/s)?
Which loop does Stringman keep on the anchor instead of across the network?
p21-l09.explain: The 50 Hz tension loop runs on the anchor itself.
options: Line tension regulation and the 40 N cut-off

p21-l09.q: How does the motion controller find the robot’s components?
p21-l09.explain: The component server registers an mDNS service.
options: They announce themselves with mDNS and serve WebSockets on port 8765

p21-l09.q: What does projecting the measured swing forward by the delay assume?
p21-l09.explain: It is a rotation by ωτ, exact only for a free pendulum.
options: That the pendulum swings freely during the delay
That the pivot is fixed forever

p21-l09.q: Delay at which the phase lag of a 0.5 m swing reaches 90° (s)?

p21-l10.q: What breaks the usual i.i.d. assumption in imitation learning?
p21-l10.explain: The clone’s mistakes take it to states the expert never visited.
options: Future observations depend on the policy’s own previous actions

p21-l10.q: Spread after 100 steps of a random walk with 1.5 cm steps (cm)?
What does DART change about the demonstrations?
p21-l10.explain: The expert has to correct the injected errors.
options: It injects noise while the expert demonstrates, so the data show recoveries
It records at a higher frame rate

p21-l10.q: Which Stringman interface should a new autonomous behaviour written in Python use?
p21-l10.explain: The observer owns connections, state and motion primitives.
options: A Maneuver registered with the AsyncObserver
Raw CAN messages to the motors

p21-l10.q: What does Neufangled recommend about swing cancellation when recording datasets?
p21-l10.explain: The policy learns what it sees; keep the same conditions.
options: Record and evaluate with it on

p21-l10.q: Why can time distortion in a dataset hurt the trained policy?
p21-l10.explain: The observation-action pairing is what the model learns.
options: Frames and commands drift apart, so the model learns actions for the wrong observations
